idiom_name: axum Router + async handler returning an Askama template (Html)
implementation_notes: In the axum/Askama stack the Router is the dispatcher (Router::new().route("/orders/{id}", get(show))), the async fn handler is the worker (extractors supply Path/State and it awaits the service layer), and rendering is template.render() wrapped in axum::response::Html or the askama_web WebTemplate IntoResponse impl, which renders and sets text/html for you; tower layers around the router hold the cross-cutting work. What replaces the classic structure is the framework's router plus the compile-time template, so view selection is a static route; a data-driven dispatcher is justified only when the mapping or the chosen view must be decided at runtime - then return an enum of templates and match on it in the handler.
pitfalls: Extractor order matters: a body-consuming extractor must come last, and a rejected extractor short-circuits with its own status instead of your error view.
A render error and a domain error are different failures; collapsing both into 500 (or unwrapping) erases the distinction the dispatcher needs for view selection.
Holding a database connection or transaction open across the render await keeps a pool ticket busy - finish the query scope before rendering.
The Router is a value composition: parameterised routes can shadow each other, so route order is part of the dispatch semantics.
